precepts.text: Arise, O Lord, let not man prevail; let the heathen be judged in thy sight. Put them in fear, O Lord, that the nations may know themselves to be but men. Selah.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail”: let not man prevail against us. Then, “let the heathen be judged in thy sight”: let the heathen nations be judged in his sight. “Put them in fear, O Lord: that the nations may know themselves to be but men.” These nations must learn that they themselves are only men. “Selah”, meaning it is true.

Then read Isaiah 33:19 again: “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” Why? Because they shall be subdued. It is “a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not understand”: that is the other nations, whose languages we do not know.

The nations have acted like gods over Israel. The Most High puts them in fear so they know they are but men, and then they are subdued and forced to worship the King. That is why we will not see that fierce people again.

precepts.text: The Lord also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble. It does not say a refuge for the oppressor, but that is what the churches teach; God is coming for the oppressed.
precepts.point: Thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway. Always. There will never be a time in America when all black and brown people, the Israelites, are successful and ruling, and that is why we need a saviour.

precepts.text: A great white throne, and from the face of him that sat on it the earth and heaven fled away.
precepts.point: Everyone will flee at the presence of Jesus Christ. Even the Romans who pierced him will be back on the scene and will wail because of him.

note.label: Psalm 9: I Will Praise the Lord With My Whole Heart

precepts.why:
David says, “When mine enemies are turned back, they shall fall and perish at thy presence. For thou hast maintained my right and my cause; thou satest in the throne judging right.” John saw that throne: “And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.”

A great white throne, and from the face of him that sat on it the earth and heaven fled away. Everyone will flee at the presence of Jesus Christ. That is the enemies falling and perishing at his presence while he sits in the throne judging right, and it is why David praises the Lord with his whole heart.

precepts.text: He has made us kings and priests; he comes with clouds, and every eye shall see him, even they that pierced him.
precepts.point: Everyone will flee at the presence of Jesus Christ. Even the Romans who pierced him will be back on the scene and will wail because of him.

note.label: Psalm 9: I Will Praise the Lord With My Whole Heart

precepts.why:
David's enemies “shall fall and perish at thy presence”, and John shows that presence arriving: “Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen.”

He comes with clouds, and every eye shall see him, even they that pierced him. The Romans who pierced him will be back on the scene and will wail because of him. All kindreds of the earth wail while his enemies are turned back.

And for us, he “hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father; to him be glory and dominion for ever and ever.” That is why David is glad and rejoices, showing forth all his marvellous works: the same presence that makes the enemies perish makes us kings and priests.

precepts.text: He that kills with the sword must be killed with the sword; here is the patience and faith of the saints.
precepts.point: The Most High will not forget what has happened to the children of Israel; he will avenge our blood. All we must do is walk in righteousness, keep the commandments, and have faith in the son Jesus Christ while the Lord revenges the blood that has been shed.

note.label: Psalm 9: I Will Praise the Lord With My Whole Heart

precepts.why:
“When he maketh inquisition for blood, he remembereth them: he forgetteth not the cry of the humble.” The Most High will not forget what has happened to the children of Israel; he will avenge our blood. John gives the rule of that vengeance: “He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.”

He that kills with the sword must be killed with the sword, and he that led us into captivity shall go into captivity. That is the inquisition for blood.

Here is the patience and the faith of the saints: all we must do is walk in righteousness, keep the commandments, and have faith in the son Jesus Christ while the Lord revenges the blood that has been shed. He is the refuge for the oppressed in times of trouble.

precepts.text: The nations were angry and God's wrath is come to reward the prophets and saints and destroy them who destroy the earth.
precepts.point: The Most High will not forget what has happened to the children of Israel; he will avenge our blood. All we must do is walk in righteousness, keep the commandments, and have faith in the son Jesus Christ while the Lord revenges the blood that has been shed.

note.label: Psalm 9: I Will Praise the Lord With My Whole Heart

precepts.why:
The Lord is “a refuge for the oppressed” and “forgetteth not the cry of the humble.” John shows the day he answers that cry: “And the nations were angry, and thy wrath is come, and the time of the dead, that they should be judged, and that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great; and shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth.”

The nations were angry and God's wrath is come, to reward the prophets and saints and them that fear his name, and to destroy them who destroy the earth. That is the inquisition for blood, when he remembers the humble who cried to him.

He has not forsaken them that seek him. Those who know his name put their trust in him, keep the commandments and have faith in Christ, and the Lord revenges the blood while the nations that destroyed the earth are destroyed.

precepts.text: In her (America) was found the blood of prophets and saints and all that were slain upon the earth.
precepts.point: The Most High will not forget what has happened to the children of Israel; he will avenge our blood. All we must do is walk in righteousness, keep the commandments, and have faith in the son Jesus Christ while the Lord revenges the blood that has been shed.

note.label: Psalm 9: I Will Praise the Lord With My Whole Heart

precepts.why:
“When he maketh inquisition for blood, he remembereth them”. Where is that blood found? “And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth.”

In her, America, was found the blood of prophets and saints and all that were slain upon the earth. The Most High will not forget what has happened to the children of Israel here; he will avenge our blood when he makes inquisition for it.

So we do not take vengeance ourselves. We walk in righteousness, keep the commandments and have faith in the son Jesus Christ, and the Lord who dwells in Zion remembers the cry of the humble and revenges the blood that has been shed.

precepts.text: Deliver yourself, O Zion, dwelling with the daughter of Babylon; he that touches you touches the apple of God's eye.
precepts.point: The Most High will not forget what has happened to the children of Israel; he will avenge our blood. All we must do is walk in righteousness, keep the commandments, and have faith in the son Jesus Christ while the Lord revenges the blood that has been shed.

note.label: Psalm 9: I Will Praise the Lord With My Whole Heart

precepts.why:
David says “they that know thy name will put their trust in thee: for thou, Lord, hast not forsaken them that seek thee.” Zechariah calls to those same people: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.”

Deliver yourself, O Zion, dwelling with the daughter of Babylon. He that touches you touches the apple of God's eye. That is why he makes inquisition for blood and does not forget the cry of the humble: what was done to Israel was done to the apple of his eye.

He is sent unto the nations which spoiled us. So the Lord is a refuge for the oppressed, and all we must do is keep the commandments and have faith in Christ while he revenges the blood that has been shed.

precepts.text: Woe to them that go down to Egypt (America) for help; the Egyptians are men and not God, and when the Lord stretches out his hand both helper and helped shall fall.
precepts.point: The nations have reigned so long that in their minds they think they are God. David prays that the Lord remind them they are nothing but men; the only reason they could do what they did to us is that we broke God's laws.

note.label: Psalm 9: I Will Praise the Lord With My Whole Heart

precepts.why:
David prays, “Put them in fear, O Lord: that the nations may know themselves to be but men.” The nations have reigned so long that in their minds they think they are God. Isaiah gives the same reminder: “Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the Lord!”

Woe to them that go down to Egypt, America, for help. “Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the Lord shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together.” The Egyptians are men and not God, and when the Lord stretches out his hand both helper and helped shall fall.

That is David's prayer: that the Lord remind them they are nothing but men. The only reason they could do what they did to us is that we broke God's laws. But “the needy shall not alway be forgotten: the expectation of the poor shall not perish for ever”, and the Lord “will arise against the house of the evildoers”.
